title: Virginia Woolf's birth chart
metaDescription: Virginia Woolf's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 5.5° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten bodies stand in Taurus — Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune and Pluto. A cluster that size stops being one voice among ten. It becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 5.5° Aquarius. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Saturn in the classical scheme — a air sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts the Sun at right angles from Saturn, 0.4° off exact. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Mercury square Jupiter at 1.4°, and Jupiter trine Uranus at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked at both ends of that civil day and survive either way, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, one sits in a sign it has an opinion about. The Sun in Aquarius at 5.5° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counted by element the chart runs 6 earth, 3 air, 1 fire, and by modality 6 fixed, 2 cardinal, 2 mutable. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. No body at all in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Mars, Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — motion that reverses only from this vantage point, and which the old reading treats as delay used for revision.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.7° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
